standard_prerequisites.name: Dg modules over a dg algebra and the category K(Mod)
standard_prerequisites.statement: The dg category of dg modules and the homotopy category obtained by identifying homotopic morphisms.
standard_prerequisites.use: The construction and its compatibility with the homotopy category are the setting (source lines 2849-2867, 2875-2892).

standard_prerequisites.name: Resolution of a dg module
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every dg module is quasi-isomorphic to one with property (P), so the derived functor can be computed from such a resolution (the author's resolution lemma, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the replacement used to define the derived functor (source lines 2869-2880).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy invariance of the Hom complex
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Hom complex depends only on the quasi-isomorphism classes involved (the author's property (P) lemma, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It shows the construction does not depend on the chosen resolution (source lines 2880-2890).

core_obligations: Set up the resolution: use the retained resolution result to replace the second variable by a quasi-isomorphic dg module with property (P), and define the derived Hom by applying the Hom construction to that representative (source lines 2869-2880).

Show independence of the resolution: invoke the retained property (P) lemma to see that a different choice gives a quasi-isomorphic answer, so the construction is well defined on the derived category (source lines 2880-2890).

Verify the derived-functor properties: check that the construction restricts to the underived Hom on the original category and is compatible with the homotopy category, concluding the existence of the right derived functor (source lines 2890-2892).

proof_roadmap.step: Replace by a property (P) resolution and define the derived Hom.
Check independence of the resolution via the homotopy-invariance lemma.
Verify the derived-functor properties and conclude.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-hom-derived at source lines 2849-2867: under the standing hypotheses the right derived functor of Hom out of a complex K is computed by replacing the second variable by a suitable resolution and then taking morphisms in the dg category, so that the derived Hom exists and is given by that construction. The proof at source lines 2869-2892 uses the resolution results of the chapter to replace a complex by a quasi-isomorphic object with the required properties, verifies that the construction is independent of the resolution up to quasi-isomorphism using the homotopy-invariance statements, and then checks the two defining properties of a derived functor: that it extends the underived functor on the original category and that it is compatible with the homotopy category. The references it uses reach other chapters (the Homology and Derived chapters) and a Homology-chapter result is named by its project tag; those targets carry canonical tags and are declared as source pointers, while everything the counted argument needs is inside the retained spans.
